title: Cohort Retention Heatmap
insights:
Dataset Summary

The dataset contains a total of 44,031 events recorded from 499 users over a date range from December 24, 2025 to January 20, 2026. There are 80 event types categorized under the application.

Cohort Retention Matrix

The retention matrix for the cohorts is as follows:

  • W1 (n=118): 100% (initial), 7.6% (W1 retention)
  • W2 (n=220): 100% (initial), 4.1% (W1 retention)
  • W3 (n=154): 100% (initial), 0.0% (W1 retention)
  • W52 (n=7): 100% (initial), 71.4% (W1 retention)

Insights

  • BEST COHORT: The cohort from week 52 has the strongest retention with a W1 retention of 71.4%. This could be attributed to seasonal factors, such as increased travel during the holiday season, or effective marketing campaigns aimed at encouraging users to book tickets during this period.
  • WORST COHORT: The cohort from week 3 shows the fastest drop-off, with a W1 retention of 0.0% and W2 retention of 0.0%. This indicates that users from this cohort did not return after their initial experience, suggesting potential issues with the app's usability or value proposition during that time.
  • OVERALL TREND: Retention appears to be declining across successive cohorts. The W1 retention rates decrease significantly from 7.6% in week 1 to 0.0% in week 3, indicating that user engagement is not improving and may be negatively impacted by product changes or a lack of compelling reasons for users to return.
  • RETENTION STRATEGIES:
    • Implement a user feedback mechanism after the first booking experience to identify pain points, as the drop-off in week 3 suggests users are not finding value in the app.
    • Enhance marketing efforts during the initial user experience, particularly for cohorts that show lower retention rates, to encourage repeat bookings and improve the overall user experience.
